quotes.text: The main reason enterprise rag fails is retrieval, not generation. When your model gives a plausible but wrong answer, it usually isn't because the model invented a lie. It's because the right context never actually made it into the prompt.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes RAG failures as retrieval problems rather than model problems.

quotes.text: The vector index itself should never surface a document the user isn't allowed to see no matter how relevant that document is to the search. Semantic similarity is a great tool for finding information but it is not an authorization mechanism.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States a clear security principle for retrieval-time access control.

quotes.text: The algorithm choice handles the cost. The pipeline design handles the quality. These are two different problems. If you confuse them, you'll end up with an architecture that is either too expensive to run or too wrong to use.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Separates the index decision (cost) from pipeline design (answer quality).

quotes.text: If you create semantically coherent chunks that follow section headings and logical units, your retrieval will improve no matter which algorithm you use.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a concrete, algorithm-independent recommendation for better retrieval.

quotes.text: A system that gives the wrong answer with total confidence is actually worse than a system that gives no answer at all.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concise argument for investing in retrieval quality and evaluation.

takeaways: HNSW keeps the whole graph in RAM and is the right choice for smaller corpora with strict latency needs, but at roughly a billion vectors it needs terabytes of memory per replica.
DiskANN keeps a compressed navigation layer in RAM and the full graph on SSD, reaching similar recall at a fraction of the memory, with Cosmos DB suited to dynamic data and SQL Server to static data.
Index choice drives cost, while answer quality depends on hybrid search, reranking, chunking, chunk-level metadata filters and continuous evaluation and observability.
hook: Vector search that looks cheap at ten million embeddings can turn into a RAM budget crisis at a billion. This episode is for Azure and AI architects building RAG and enterprise search on Azure AI Search, Cosmos DB or SQL Server. You get a practical framework for choosing between HNSW and DiskANN based on scale, update frequency, latency and cost.
